entries.what_happened: The manuscript 'A Complete Local Domain without a Small Cohen–Macaulay Module' (OpenAI, dated 23 September 2026) claims a three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain R containing ℂ, with residue field ℂ, that has no nonzero finitely generated module of depth 3 (equal to dim R), i.e. no small (maximal) Cohen–Macaulay module. This is the domain form of the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture, which is item (14) of the list's named homological conjectures. The ring is R(X,H), the completion at its homogeneous maximal ideal of T(X,H) = ⊕ H⁰(X, jH), for a smooth projective complex surface X with an ample globally generated H. The specific pair used has n = 7: X is an abelian (ℤ/7)⁵ Kummer cover of the blow-up of ℙ² at four points, branched along the six lines joining them and the four exceptional curves, with H² = 1715. Non-existence is derived from a numerical obstruction (Theorem 1.2 in the manuscript): if R(X,H) admits a small Cohen–Macaulay module then K_X² − 2c₂(X) ≤ 6H², which the chosen surface violates (13377 > 10290). The manuscript also claims a corollary that the uncompleted localisation T_𝔫 is a three-dimensional local domain essentially of finite type over ℂ with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module.
entries.delivers: If the claim holds, it refutes the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture in the list's form. The list asks for a nonzero finitely generated module on which some (equivalently every) system of parameters is regular, for every complete local ring. The ring here is a complete local ring with no such module, so the counterexample refutes the list's form. The manuscript itself states only the domain form ('every complete Noetherian local domain has one'), which is a special case of the list's statement, so the two statements do not match word for word; the implication to the list's form is not stated in the text. Restrictions: the counterexample is a normal domain of dimension three in equal characteristic zero (it contains ℂ with residue field ℂ). The non-existence is only for finitely generated modules; the manuscript says big Cohen–Macaulay modules exist and are not affected. The proof uses only the n = 7 member of the surface family. The corollary gives a counterexample in the class of three-dimensional local domains essentially of finite type over ℂ.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, item (14) is settled negatively and nothing in it remains open. Items (1)–(13) of the list's named conjectures (Zero Divisor, Bass's question, Intersection, New Intersection, Improved New Intersection, Direct Summand, Canonical Element, balanced big Cohen–Macaulay existence, Cohen–Macaulayness of direct summands of regular rings, Tor vanishing, Strong Direct Summand, weakly functorial big Cohen–Macaulay algebras, and Serre's multiplicity conjecture) are not addressed by this manuscript, which cites several of them as already known. The Peskine–Szpiro, Huneke–Şega–Vraciu, Huneke–Wiegand, and Auslander–Reiten/Nakayama/Tachikawa conjectures are not discussed in the text.
entries.direction: disproves the conjecture (domain form, and so the list's form)
entries.object: R = completion of T(X,H) at its homogeneous maximal ideal, where X is a specific surface: the abelian (ℤ/7)⁵ Kummer cover of the blow-up of ℙ² at four points, branched along six joining lines and four exceptional curves, and H = 3J − E with H² = 1715. The ring is explicitly defined by this construction, but the manuscript does not write out its generators or relations, and the non-existence of a small Cohen–Macaulay module is proved by contradiction from the Chern-number obstruction, not by an explicit check on modules.
entries.doubts: Lemma 3.1 (the slope-balancing modification) is adapted from Chen–Sun's analytic setting, which the manuscript says differs in its hypotheses; the authors 'recall briefly' the Harder–Narasimhan filtration and give the termination argument in a few sentences. Several structural steps are argued in outline: the depth-inequality step that CM modules of full support localise to CM modules, the depth bound for coherent duals on regular schemes, the regularity of the models V and W, and the étale local normal form of the cover in Lemma cover-smooth, which is argued with 'after an étale base change' steps. The surface section cites Anghel2026 §7.2 as the source of the construction, but says all required numerical and positivity checks are carried out directly in the manuscript.

entries.not_relevant_because: The manuscript never mentions the monomial conjecture or powers of parameter ideals. Its result refutes the existence of a finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over one ring, but such a module is only a sufficient route to the monomial conjecture, so its failure does not decide the conjecture. The manuscript cites big Cohen–Macaulay algebra existence for Noetherian local rings as known, and makes no claim about the monomial conjecture for R.
